The P1 incident (ENG-186) was caused by a **misconfigured `max.poll.interval.ms` (30 min) in the Kafka consumer properties** of the telemetry-ingestion service. The service expects to poll at least every 5 seconds; the inflated interval made the broker declare the consumer stalled, triggering rebalances and message backlog [source:CONF-ENG-260]. The Jira ticket confirms the same: "Misconfigured max.poll.interval.ms caused Kafka consumer lag, stalling the telemetry-ingestion Spring Boot service and breaching the sub‑100 ms latency target" [source:ENG-186]. That misconfiguration was introduced by a **deployment**, not discovered/missed through a missing page of docs.

## How the Jax/Raj/Kaitlyn gaps actually relate

- **Kaitlyn / PR-101 (2026-01-06, tied to ENG-101):** the PR's gap_areas are "mobile analytics; legacy auth service; AWS cost structure; Project Titan" [source:PR-101, source:ENG-101]. These map directly to the *downstream impact* columns of the postmortem (delayed mobile analytics, legacy auth latency, ~$4,200 AWS overage, Project Titan pipeline stall) [source:CONF-ENG-260]. Closing that doc gap would have improved visibility of impact, not prevented the bad config from shipping.
- **Raj (PR-134 / PR-118, mobile side):** the mobile telemetry-streaming and in-app alert work [source:PR-134, source:PR-118] is orthogonal to the backend Kafka consumer misconfig — Raj's gaps touch the consuming UI/transport layer, not the `max.poll.interval.ms` setting.
- **Jax (you):** the closest artifact is your PR-119 fix for a *different* misconfiguration (consumer group offset reset policy) [source:PR-119], and your later PR-143 which actually fixed the ENG-230 recurrence of this same bug [source:PR-143].

## The real "would-have-prevented" gaps

The postmortem and sprint retro make clear the higher-leverage failures were: no config-drift guard on the Kafka consumer, no root-cause write-up culture, and incomplete scaling/threshold tickets [source:CONF-RETRO-001, source:CONF-ENG-260]. Closing your doc gap on Day 4 would not have changed any of those mechanics.
